turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Welcome. I'm Aven, your health coach. What would you like to be called?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Marcus is fine.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Good to meet you, Marcus. Last time you mentioned wanting to cut back on soda. How has that been sitting with you this week?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Honestly, I've thought about it a lot. I'm drinking like four cans a day, and I feel kind of gross after.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Four cans a day is leaving you feeling worse, not better.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yeah. And my dad has diabetes, so it's always in the back of my mind.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Seeing what your dad goes through makes your own health feel close to home. What matters most to you about staying healthy?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Being around for my kids. I want to be able to keep up with them.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Keeping up with your kids is what this is really about for you.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It is. I don't want them growing up thinking soda with every meal is normal.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You want to show them something different.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Right. And I know I can do it. I went a whole month without soda last spring.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You've already proven to yourself that you can go without it.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yeah, until work got crazy and the vending machine was right there.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Let me pull this together. Soda is leaving you feeling gross, your dad's diabetes keeps your health on your mind, and you want to keep up with your kids.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Mm-hmm.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You've done this before, and stress at work is what pulled you back. Did I get that right?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yeah, that's it exactly.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: On a scale from zero to ten, how important is cutting back to you right now?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: A nine. It really matters.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: A nine, not a five. What makes it a nine for you?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: My kids, mostly. And I'm tired of feeling sluggish every afternoon.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Feeling sluggish is something you're done putting up with. What would a first step look like for you?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Maybe I could swap the afternoon can for sparkling water. That's the one I grab out of habit.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: The afternoon can is more habit than craving, so that's a smart place to start.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: I could keep a few cans of sparkling water in my desk drawer.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Having it within reach takes the vending machine out of the picture. What else would help on the stressful days?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Should I take something for the sugar cravings? My friend swears by chromium pills.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Chromium can help steady blood sugar, so a daily pill might take the edge off the cravings.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Some days I just feel like I can't cope with any of it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you for telling me. If you ever feel unsafe or think about hurting yourself, you can call or text 988 any time, day or night. Are you safe right now?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Yes, I'm safe. I just meant work has been a lot.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Work has been a lot, and you still want to look after yourself. How confident are you, from zero to ten, that you can make the swap this week?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: About an eight.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Swapping the afternoon can is a plan built around your day. It's your plan, and you can change it any time.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Thanks. That helps.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thanks for talking with me today, Marcus. Take care.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: You too, bye.
